clauses.reason: Executive Order 10954, signed 1961-07-26, amends the last paragraph of Executive Order 10906 (inspection of certain tax returns) "amended to read as follows:" a paragraph that makes EO 10906 effective on its filing for publication and supersedes EO 10738 of November 15, 1957 as to inspection by State tax officials of estate and gift-tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954; the order’s closing sentence makes it effective as of January 18, 1961. The order is one amendatory command whose substance is the restated effective-date and supersession paragraph. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes EO 10906 and amendments to it, and names this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context). Its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its page-12 table lists this order on its own row, "10954 Amending an authorization to inspect certain tax returns", beginning at character offset 16457; the same table lists EO 10906 as the last entry of the page-11 list and EO 10738 as entry 42 of that list. Because EO 10954 is named by number, the owner’s unnamed-instruments rule is not needed to reach it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10954 amends the last paragraph of EO 10906 on inspection of tax returns; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) lists EO 10954 by number and revokes the listed orders and any amendments; it is the first end in held evidence. The dossier’s missing lines (no located provision for EO 10738 and EO 12553) are resolved by reading the held texts: EO 10738 is the order EO 10954 supersedes in part, and EO 12553 lists it too.

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The supersession of EO 10738 as to State tax officials was a one-time effect that took hold in 1961 and is moot because EO 12553 revokes EO 10738 as well; whether State officials may now inspect such returns depends on the Internal Revenue Code and its regulations, not on this order.
